title: The Fox and the Crow
style: Layered paper-craft illustration: cut paper collage with soft drop shadows between layers and visible paper fibre texture, warm muted palette (sage green, mustard yellow, terracotta, soft blue, cream), gentle children's storybook look. Vertical 9:16, 1080x1920. The top 22% is plain cream sky (only a paper sun and one small paper cloud) so a caption fits there. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark. Every frame uses the same wide camera angle and the same layout: one big oak tree on the left with a long branch reaching right, meadow with wildflowers, soft green hills behind, sun top right (unless the scene says close).
characters: CROW: glossy blue-black paper crow with a yellow-grey beak and small shiny eyes, holding a pinkish-red piece of meat in her beak until it falls. FOX: slim orange-red paper fox with white chest and tail tip, black paws, pointed ears, clever friendly eyes. Same meadow setting in every frame.

sentences.en: A crow sits on a branch with a piece of meat.
sentences.tr: Bir karga, gagasında bir parça etle bir dalda oturur.
sentences.scene: Wide view: the black crow sits on a high branch of the oak tree holding a piece of meat in her beak; the fox is not there yet.

sentences.en: A fox sees the meat and wants it.
sentences.tr: Bir tilki eti görür ve onu ister.
sentences.scene: Same wide view: the orange fox stands at the foot of the oak tree, looking up hungrily at the crow and the meat.

sentences.en: He cannot climb up to take it.
sentences.scene: Same wide view: the fox stands on his hind legs with front paws on the tree trunk, trying to climb, but the branch is far too high.

sentences.en: So he begins to praise the crow.
sentences.scene: Same wide view: the fox sits below the tree, smiling sweetly up at the crow, one paw raised as if giving a compliment.

sentences.en: “What beautiful feathers you have!” he says.
sentences.scene: Close on the crow on the branch, the fox's admiring face small below; little paper sparkles around the crow's glossy blue-black feathers.

sentences.en: “You must have a beautiful voice, too.”
sentences.scene: Same wide view: the fox puts a paw on his chest and points up at the crow with a charming smile; paper music notes float near the crow.
The crow on the branch puffs up her chest proudly, eyes half closed, head held high, still holding the meat.

sentences.en: She wants to show him her voice.
sentences.scene: The crow spreads her wings a little and lifts her head, ready to sing, the meat still in her beak; the fox watches eagerly below.

sentences.en: She opens her beak and makes a loud sound.
sentences.tr: Gagasını açar ve yüksek bir ses çıkarır.
sentences.scene: The crow opens her beak wide and caws loudly; big paper sound waves come out; the meat starts to slip from her beak.

sentences.en: The meat falls to the ground.
sentences.scene: Same wide view: the piece of meat falls through the air toward the ground; the crow looks shocked, beak open.

sentences.en: The fox picks it up and laughs.
sentences.scene: Same wide view: the fox catches the meat in his mouth on the ground and laughs, eyes closed with joy; the crow stares from the branch.

sentences.en: “You have a voice, but you need more sense,” he says.
sentences.tr: “Sesin var ama daha akıllı olman gerekiyor,” der.
sentences.scene: The fox looks up at the crow with the meat in his mouth, one paw raised like a teacher giving advice; the crow looks ashamed.

sentences.en: The crow watches him leave with her meal.
sentences.scene: Same wide view: the fox trots away to the right with the meat; the crow watches sadly from the branch.
Calm wide view: the crow alone on the branch at sunset, thinking; one small paper leaf falls.

quiz.say_tr: Sence “praise” ne demek? Övmek mi, uçmak mı, saklamak mı?
